itens.titulo: Intel Shares Plunge 25% as Weak Fourth-Quarter Outlook Overshadows Strong Q3 Earnings
itens.descricao: Intel Shares Plunge 25% as Weak Fourth-Quarter Outlook Overshadows Strong Q3 Earnings Yahoo Finance
trechos: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) shares fell 25% in premarket trading after the semiconductor manufacturer issued fourth-quarter revenue and earnings forecasts significantly below Wall Street expectations, despite reporting stronger-than-anticipated third-quarter results.
The company reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share, exceeding analysts' expectations of $0.40.
Revenue increased 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, slightly ahead of the consensus estimate of $16.48 billion.

Fourth-Quarter Revenue and Earnings Forecasts Miss Expectations Intel projected fourth-quarter revenue of between $15 billion and $16 billion, considerably below the $17.08 billion anticipated by analysts.
The midpoint of the company's forecast, at $15.5 billion, represents a shortfall of approximately 9% compared with market expectations.
Intel also expects adjusted earnings of $0.25 per share for the quarter, compared with the consensus forecast of $0.44.
"Despite near-term headwinds across the PC industry, demand for our CPUs remains robust," Tan said.

PC Market Weakness Expected to Continue Into 2027 Intel's Client Computing and Physical AI Group reported third-quarter revenue of $8.1 billion, representing a 5% decline from the same period last year.

itens.titulo: Intel plunges on a major guidance miss. What went wrong — and how to proceed
itens.descricao: Intel plunges on a major guidance miss. What went wrong — and how to proceed CNBC
trechos: Revenue in the third quarter increased 21% year over year to $16.513 billion, edging out the LSEG-compiled consensus estimate of $16.496 billion.
Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) more than doubled to 52 cents, beating the LSEG estimate of 40 cents.
As a result, our rating is currently under review, and we are slashing our price target to $100.
"The industry continues to navigate one of the most significant supply shortages in history driven by the unprecedented demand for superintelligence," CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on the conference call.

Sales in the unit fell 5% year-over-year, but it still accounts for more than half of the revenue of Intel's products group (CCPG + DCAI) and about 43% of Intel Products' operating income (see chart below).
That PC exposure is weighing on Intel's outlook for the rest of the year, even as it reported its strongest DCAI (data center and AI) segment growth in 15 years.
"In recent weeks, our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on the memory prices and availability," Tan said.

CEO Tan said demand for 2027 is "significant, especially in CPU-dense rack-scale infrastructure." However, if Intel is going to capitalize on the opportunity, it needs to ramp up its manufacturing capacity.

itens.titulo: Could $1,000 Invested in Palantir Turn Into $100,000?
itens.descricao: Could $1,000 Invested in Palantir Turn Into $100,000? Yahoo Finance
trechos: A $1,000 investment at its earliest trading price of $10 would be worth about $19,400 today.
That's an impressive six-year gain, but could it eventually turn that investment into $100,000?
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
From 2021 to 2025, Palantir's revenue grew at a 31% CAGR.
It also turned profitable in 2023 and grew its EPS at a 165% CAGR over the following two years.
From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Palantir's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 59% and 70%, respectively.
However, its stock isn't cheap at 91 times next year's earnings.

itens.titulo: Petrobras anuncia nova descoberta de petróleo na Foz do Amazonas
itens.descricao: Petrobras anuncia nova descoberta de petróleo na Foz do Amazonas Agência Brasil
itens.texto:
Mais uma descoberta de petróleo em águas ultraprofundas na costa do estado do Amapá, Foz do Amazonas.
O anúncio foi feito pela Petrobras nessa quinta-feira.
A descoberta foi no poço Morpho, a cerca de 175 km da costa do estado do Amapá e a quase 2.900 m de profundidade.
Segundo a Petrobras, a confirmação da nova fonte de petróleo é consequência da avaliação de outros intervalos de interesse, após duas descobertas anteriores, divulgadas em agosto e em outubro deste ano.
A presidente da Petrobras, Magda Chambriard, disse que as três descobertas deixam a empresa mais otimista em relação ao potencial exploratório da área.
A perfuração e a coleta de dados geológicos já foram concluídas no poço Morpho.
Agora, a sonda será transferida para a Bacia Potiguar, a cerca de 50 km da costa do Rio Grande do Norte, onde deve começar a perfuração na locação Mãe de Ouro.
A presidente da Petrobras também ressaltou os resultados operacionais da empresa, divulgados na quarta-feira.
No terceiro trimestre, a produção média, incluindo óleo e gás natural, alcançou a marca recorde de 3 milhões e meio de barris por dia, 5,3% acima do segundo trimestre desse ano.
De acordo com a empresa, a atuação da Petrobras na margem equatorial, que fica entre os estados do Amapá e o Rio Grande do Norte, está alinhada à estratégia de recompor as reservas de petróleo e gás por meio da exploração de novas fronteiras.
A empresa já perfurou mais de 700 poços por lá.
